Then he came to his mother. She said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am your son!" Then she recognized his speech and rejoiced. He stretched the bow. Then he slew the men who were devouring his cattle, and he became king. His fame is good.

pie: wĺ̥kʷōs h₂éwibʰos wr̥h₁ént. h₂óweyes wos ḱwónes gʰósteyes h₁sénti. n̥sméy tóns dh₃té usmé-kʷe ne h₁édomes. téh₂es h₂óweyes tóysōm wékʷos ḱléwsont tóybʰos-kʷe tóns ḱwónn̥s h₁opéyetom. nu tóy tóns moréyont tā́s-kʷe gʷmént. téh₂es h₂óweyes trésont tóybʰos-kʷe bʰh₂ént. wĺ̥kʷōs n̥smé mē gʷr̥h₃éte. tóy skʷént. tóy ḱwónes lelikʷḗr kʷís-kʷe usmé h₂léksēti? nu tā́s gʷr̥h₃ónt. tóy sh₂ént. h₁yós tóybʰos wĺ̥kʷoybʰos tósyo ḱwónn̥s déh₃eti tóy tóm h₁dénti.
english: Wolves said to sheep: "Sheep, the dogs are your enemies. Give them to us, and we will not eat you." The sheep listened to their word and gave them the dogs. Then they killed them and came to the sheep. The sheep trembled in fear and spoke to them: "Wolves, do not devour us!" They said: "The dogs are gone, and who will protect you?" Then they devoured them. They were sated. Whoever gives his dogs to the wolves, they eat him.

pie: owis, yāi wl̥nā ne eest, dedorḱe eḱwons, tom woǵʰom gʷr̥um weǵʰontm̥, tom bʰorom meǵm̥, tom ǵʰm̥onm̥ ōku bʰerontm̥.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: wiHrós yemHós-kʷe témHesi tḱyént. dʰéǵʰōm ne h₁ést dyḗws-kʷe ne h₁ést. témHos bʰénǵʰu h₁ést. nu wiHrós yemHṓy wéwket. dʰéǵʰōm tḗtḱomes. yemHós h₂éǵt. bʰréh₂ter me h₁yáǵye. nu só tóm noḱéyet dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe tósyo mémsh₁ démet dyḗm-kʷe tósyo h₂n̥téh₁ tḗtḱt. sóh₂wl̥ tósyo gʷʰéresh₁ tḗtḱt. nu só tósyeh₂i ǵʰémi stéh₂t némos-kʷe stoh₂éyet. péh₂wr̥ tósmi némesi stnéh₂t. só yemHós mr̥téys h₃rḗǵs bʰúHt tósyo-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁ésti. tóy wiHrṓs wiHrósyo népotes h₁sénti.
english: Man and Twin dwelt in darkness. Earth was not, and sky was not. Darkness was thick. Then Man said to Twin: "Let us create the earth!" Twin said: "Brother, sacrifice me!" Then he killed him, and with his flesh he built the earth, and with his forehead he created the sky. With his heat he created the sun. Then he stood up on the earth and set up a place of sacrifice. In the place of sacrifice he placed fire. Twin became the king of death, and his name is famous. Men are the grandsons of Man.

pie: wédnōm népōts pl̥h₁nóy déh₂n̥wi tḱéyti. só h₁n̥gʷnís h₁ésti tód-kʷe déh₂nu tóm ḱéleti. só tósmi dʰégʷʰeti. kʷís tóm dedórḱe? wiHrṓs tóm ne dedr̥ḱḗr. nu tóy péh₂wr̥ h₂isḱónt sréwmn̥-kʷe gʷh₂ént. tósmey sruméney wérh₁yont. sréwmn̥ n̥sméy péh₂wr̥ dédh₃dʰi. nu tód tóybʰos tóm népotm̥ h₁opéyet só-kʷe tóns gʷʰr̥néwt tóy-kʷe swidyónt. mḗms pékʷont tód-kʷe h₁dént tóy-kʷe tr̥pént. tóy tósmey h₁yáǵyont. só népōts h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr h₁ésti. wédnōm népot n̥sméy h₁wésuh₂ dh₃dʰí.
english: The Grandson of the Waters dwells in the full river. He is Fire, and the river hides him. He burns in it. Who has seen him? Men have not seen him. Then they sought fire and went to a stream. They were saying to the stream: "Stream, give us fire!" Then it gave them the Grandson, and he warmed them, and they sweated. They cooked meat and ate it, and they were sated. They sacrificed to him. The Grandson is the giver of good things. Grandson of the Waters, give us good things!

pie: sruméni sth₂éh₁yontih₂ h₂ówis h₁éḱwons widét. tóy méǵh₂m̥ kʷékʷlom duként wiHróm-kʷe wéǵʰont. séh₂ h₂ówis tóybʰos mléwHt. h₁éḱwōs só wiHrós usmé déwkti tóm-kʷe wéǵʰete. tóm ne bʰebʰih₂é? tóy h₂ǵént. ḱléwse h₂ówi. tóm ne bʰebʰih₂mé. só n̥sméy wódr̥ dédeh₃ti téwe-kʷe mḗms pékʷeti. nu séh₂ tód ḱléwsontih₂ h₂ówis h₂éǵrom dréh₂t. h₁yós wiHróm wóyde só tóm bʰebʰóyh₂e.
english: A sheep standing at a stream saw horses. They were drawing a great wagon and carrying a man. The sheep said to them: "Horses, the man leads you, and you carry him. Do you not fear him?" They said: "Listen, sheep! We do not fear him. He gives us water, and he cooks your flesh." Then the sheep, hearing this, ran away into the field. He who knows man fears him.

pie: "tód h₁estu", wéwked lewkós deywós wérunos.
english: "Let this be so," said the bright god Werunos.

pie: yemHṓs HéHḱuns h₁éḱwons h₂éǵonti. tóysōm h₁éḱwōs pléwonti tóysōm-kʷe kʷékʷlos HéHḱus h₁ésti. h₂éwsōs diwés dʰugh₂tḗr tóysōm swésōr h₁ésti. h₂egʷnós Hreh₁móy sruméni séngʷt tóybʰos-kʷe wérh₁t. yemHṓs me h₂léksete. mértis me gʷr̥h₃éti. nu tósyo wékʷos ḱl̥wént tóm-kʷe h₁l̥h₂ént. nu tóm tl̥nh₂ént tóm-kʷe tósmi kʷékʷloy sodéyont. só stéwdt tóm-kʷe gʷʰr̥nwént. só méwdt tóybʰos-kʷe yemHóybʰos sékʷt. ḱléwos wos méǵh₂ h₁ésti. h₁nómn̥ wos ḱlutóm h₁syéh₁t.
english: The Twins drive swift horses. Their horses fly, and their chariot is swift. Dawn, daughter of Sky, is their sister. A lamb sank in a dark stream, and it said to them: "Twins, protect me! Death is swallowing me!" Then they heard its word and drove to it. Then they lifted it and seated it in the chariot. It had grown cold, and they warmed it. It rejoiced and said to the Twins: "Your fame is great. May your name be famous!"

pie: h₃rḗǵs Hyudʰsmóybʰos bʰéh₂t. Hyudʰsmṓs méne wékʷos ḱléwsete. gʰósteyes nos h₂éǵrons h₂eh₂n̥ḱḗr gʷówn̥s-kʷe nos stéh₂yonti. gʷéruh₂ gʰr̥bh₂té kʷékʷloybʰos-kʷe h₁éḱwons yungté. tóns térh₂womes. tóns gʷéh₂omes tóns-kʷe noḱéyōmes. h₁yós kh₃téwi séngʷeti tósyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti. h₁yós dréh₂eti ḱwónes tóm h₁édonti. nu tóy tósyo h₃réǵs wékʷos ḱl̥wént tóns-kʷe dr̥mént.
english: The king spoke to the warriors: "Warriors, listen to my word! The enemies have reached our fields, and they are stealing our cattle. Seize the spears and join the horses to the chariots! Let us overcome them! Let us go to them and let us kill them! Whoever falls in the battle, his fame will be imperishable. Whoever runs away, the dogs will eat him." Then they heard the king's word and ran to them.

pie: méh₂tēr déywih₂ suHnówey mléwHt. h₁yód kéh₃tum gʷéh₂esi mértis te kapyḗti téwe-kʷe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti. h₁yód téwe ph₂trés ph₂wéni sísdēsi téwe népotn̥s widḗsi téwe-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm ne h₁éseti. nu só h₂éǵt. méh₂ter tóm kéh₃tum gʷéh₂oh₂. mértis me sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t méne-kʷe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁syéh₁t. nu néwōy kʷékʷlōy h₁éḱwons yunégt tóm-kʷe kéh₃tum h₁élh₂t. tósyo h₁éḱwōs pléwont. séh₂ tóm spéḱyet séh₂-kʷe trémt. séh₂ tósyo h₁nómn̥ memóne.
english: A mother, a goddess, said to her son: "If you go to the battle, death will grasp you, and your fame will be imperishable. If you sit at your father's fire, you will see your grandsons, and your name will not be famous." Then he said: "Mother, I shall go to the battle. May death take me, and may my fame be imperishable!" Then he joined horses to a new chariot and drove to the battle. His horses flew. She kept looking at him, and she trembled. She remembers his name.
